content.title: The Twelfth Mooring
content.subtitle: A Hebridean Mystery
content.summary: Mara Quinn comes home to Calder after her father's boat fails to return. She finds a pencilled word in the harbour log and a boatman who will not meet her eye. Each chapter peels back a layer of the island's silence until she learns her father staged his disappearance to protect her from a debt, and she chooses to tell the island the truth.
content.targetAudience: Adult readers who like slow-burn island mysteries.
uniqueSellingPoints: a missing father, not a body
a heroine who solves it by listening
content.toneNotes: Spare, wind-blown and exact. Short scenes, few adjectives.

storyBible.logline: A harbourmaster's daughter must find her missing father before the island decides he chose to leave.
themes: loyalty to family against loyalty to the truth
a small place keeping its secrets

characters.name: Mara Quinn
characters.need: to trust people outside her family
characters.voiceNotes: short, dry sentences; never says sorry
characters.appearance: 32, tall, salt-stiff dark hair, her father's old oilskin coat

characters.name: Tomas Reyes
characters.need: to admit what he saw on Sunday
characters.voiceNotes: jokes when cornered, answers questions with questions
characters.appearance: 50s, broad, grey beard, rope burns on both hands

settings.name: Calder Harbour
settings.description: a stone harbour on a small Hebridean island, twelve moorings, a slipway and a one-room harbour office

settings.name: The harbour office
settings.description: smells of paraffin and old paper; the logbook lives under the barometer

timeline: Sunday: the Gannet goes out at six
Sunday night: the Gannet does not come back
Tuesday: Mara arrives on the morning ferry
storyBible.povPlan: Close third person, past tense, every chapter from Mara's point of view.
storyBible.ending: Mara learns her father staged his disappearance to protect her from a debt, and chooses to tell the island the truth.

chapters.title: Eleven
chapters.summary: Mara arrives and finds a mooring empty. Tomas is evasive. In the harbour office she finds the pencilled word in the log.
scenes: Mara counts eleven moorings and meets Tomas on the slipway
Mara finds the word Wait in the logbook
chapters.openingHookIdea: The tide turning and the boat missing
chapters.bridgeToNext: Who wrote the word in pencil?

chapters.title: Wait
chapters.summary: Mara compares handwriting and confronts Tomas, who admits he saw the Gannet heading north, not south.
scenes: Mara compares the pencil with old entries
chapters.openingHookIdea: Mara tilting the page to the light again

content.backCoverBlurb: When her father's boat fails to come home, Mara Quinn takes the first ferry back to Calder. The island says he chose to go. The harbour log says something else.
content.amazonDescriptionDraft: When her father's boat fails to come home, Mara Quinn returns to the island she left.
claimsToWatch: sea safety and coastguard procedure in chapter 2
